newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta holds firm vs mark but capped near 84.10.
newsitem.headline: Peseta holds firm vs mark but capped near 84.10.

text.p: The peseta held firm against the mark in morning trade on Tuesday, brushing aside strong gains in bonds amid expectations that the Bank of Spain would intervene around 84.10 per mark, traders said.
They said the narrow ranges seen in recent sessions were set to persist short-term.
"We could be looking at a range of 84.05 to 84.25 even up to Christmas unless, for example, it becomes clear that we won't make the Maastricht criteria," said one trader.
By 1200 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.15/17 versus early levels of 84.17/19 and late Monday levels of 84.18/20.

"It appears that the market is assuming that the Bank of Spain wants to cut short any further appreciation towards 84.10 per mark, and at the moment this psychological barrier is sufficient to prevent any further gains," said one trader.
Spanish balance of payments data due this week were unlikely to shake the peseta too aggressively, traders said.
Instead the market was looking toward U.S. data. Tuesday sees the release of U.S. housing starts for October. But traders said U.S. trade data on Wednesday would be more interesting.
Traders said they would also watch for further Bundesbank comments after Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that a stable, stronger dollar was preferable.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen is due to speak at 1400 GMT today and Welteke is scheduled to speak again at 1900 GMT.
